title: Azure Southeast Asia 2023: Chillers Hang After a Dip, Then Lock Out
dcName: Southeast Asia Availability Zone datacenter (not named)

severity.usersAffected: Customers in one Southeast Asia zone across about 30 services and the Azure portal; ARM management failures in Southeast Asia and East Asia; Site Recovery, Backup and GRS failover problems.
severity.tier: One Availability Zone, with control-plane effects in two regions

brief: On 7 February 2023 a voltage dip tripped chillers at an Azure Southeast Asia zone in Singapore. Three chillers, over half the capacity, hung on a control-card fault the procedure did not cover; by the time it was reset the loop was too hot and they locked out. The zone was shut down from 20:19 UTC until the next day, and ARM and BCDR services failed with it.

magnitude.note: One zone, with management impact in two regions. Duration (7): 32 h 11 min of customer impact, inside the 1–3 d band.

sequenceOfEvents.event: A utility voltage dip hits one Southeast Asia Availability Zone in Singapore; power systems ride through, but a subset of chillers trips and shuts down.
Chiller 5 is already offline for planned maintenance. Chiller 4 keeps running and chillers 1–3 restart, but chillers 6, 7 and 8 from the second supplier will not start.
The documented emergency operating procedure is run on the tripped chillers, but the manual restarts fail.
The chiller HMI shows a phase sequence alarm; the compressor control card has stopped responding and needs a hard reset with at least 5 minutes powered off, a step the procedure did not list.
Non-critical infrastructure is shut down to slow the temperature rise, and technicians from the chiller supplier are dispatched to site.
By the time the control cards are reset with the supplier, the chilled-water loop is above 28°C and the chillers enter thermal lockout.
Thermal warnings direct a shutdown of critical compute, network and storage in the zone; resources there become unavailable.
ARM in Southeast Asia loses part of its metadata store, a Cosmos DB instance in the failed zone that should have been zone-resilient but was not because of a configuration error.
Azure Site Recovery failovers fail because a recently updated workflow uses a non-zonal Service Bus instance in the failed zone.
ARM endpoints in Southeast Asia are manually removed from the global Traffic Manager profile.
The shifted ARM traffic overloads East Asia, extending management failures to that region.
The new Site Recovery workflow is disabled in Southeast Asia, ending the Service Bus failures.
Augmented cooling is brought in and IT load is reduced until the loop falls below the lockout threshold; chillers 6, 7 and 8 restart.
Microsoft proactively enables cross-region restore for all Azure Backup customers with geo-redundant vaults; a regional configuration issue then blocks some restores until 15:10.
ARM in East Asia is scaled up and fully recovered; Site Recovery failovers work reliably from 09:15.
With all chillers back, temperatures return within operational thresholds.
Power is restored in phases, storage first and then compute once storage is verified healthy.
Most customers see platform services recover.
One SQL Database tenant ring does not reform: a BIOS bug stops its hosts recovering, then a Service Fabric heap-memory issue needs manual intervention.
The final SQL Database tenant ring becomes available and the incident ends.

rootCause:
TRIGGER: at 15:17 UTC on 7 February 2023 a utility voltage dip hit one Azure Southeast Asia Availability Zone in Singapore. Power systems rode through, but several chillers tripped.

COOLING CHAIN: the plant had eight chillers from two suppliers. Chiller 5 was down for maintenance. Chillers 1–4 ran or restarted, but 6, 7 and 8, over half the capacity, would not start automatically or by the emergency procedure. Their compressor control cards had stopped responding after the dip and needed a hard power-off of at least five minutes, which the procedure did not include. By the time the supplier's technicians had reset them, the loop water was above 28°C and the chillers locked themselves out. The zone's critical equipment was shut down at 20:19.

PLATFORM CHAIN: the loss of one zone spread. ARM's metadata store was on a Cosmos DB instance wrongly configured as non-zonal, so management failed in the region; moving ARM traffic away overloaded East Asia. Site Recovery and Backup, the services meant for this situation, had their own non-zonal dependencies and configuration faults.

LATENT ROOT: a chiller control fault without a documented recovery step, a plant already one chiller down, and resilience services that were not themselves resilient to a zone loss.
contributingFactors: A utility voltage dip tripped a subset of chillers (Azure PIR).
Compressor control cards on chillers 6–8 stopped responding and needed a cold reset that the emergency procedure did not list (Azure PIR).
Chiller 5 was already offline for planned maintenance, reducing spare capacity (Azure PIR).
Once the loop exceeded 28°C the chillers entered thermal lockout and could not restart (Azure PIR).
ARM's metadata store in the region was not zone-resilient because of a configuration error (Azure PIR).
Moving ARM traffic to East Asia exceeded its capacity, spreading impact to a second region (Azure PIR).
Site Recovery depended on a non-zonal Service Bus instance in the failed zone after a recent update (Azure PIR).
A BIOS bug and a Service Fabric memory issue kept one SQL tenant ring down until 04:30 on 9 February (Azure PIR).

coe.action: Work with the chiller OEM to prevent, shorten and reliably recover these events
Add the manual cold restart of chillers to the procedures, as the OEM recommends
OEM training for datacenter operations staff on the updated procedures
Validate ARM configuration in Southeast Asia and that all ARM instances are zone/region redundant
Ensure ARM capacity in all regions can absorb traffic from zonal or regional failures
Daily automated walk of the dependency graph of zonal services to close single points of failure
Correct the Backup cross-region-restore configuration in all regions; return Site Recovery to a zone-resilient workflow
Adjust safety-check thresholds for customer-initiated GRS storage failover
Give a recoverability expectation and timeline in incident communications

lessonsLearnt: An emergency procedure is only as good as its rarest step; the cold reset the chillers needed was not written down.
Running a plant with a chiller out for maintenance removes the margin that would absorb a restart failure.
Thermal lockout turns minutes into hours; bring temporary cooling and shed load before the loop reaches the lockout limit.
Business-continuity services must be the most zone-resilient part of the platform, not the least.
Shifting a control plane to a neighbour region needs headroom there, or the failure moves with the traffic.
Zone-redundant workloads stayed largely available; regional services with hidden zonal dependencies did not.
improvements: Cooling: OEM cold-restart step added to procedures, with training (Microsoft, completed).
Control plane: ARM zone redundancy validated and spare capacity in all regions (Microsoft, completed).
BCDR: Site Recovery workflow and Backup restore configuration fixed; storage failover checks adjusted (Microsoft, completed).
Architecture: daily dependency-graph walk for zonal services (Microsoft, ongoing).
Analyst recommendation (not in the PIR): treat a chiller out for maintenance as a reduced-redundancy state with a pre-staged temporary cooling plan.

comprehensiveAnalysis.heading: Half the plant would not start
comprehensiveAnalysis.body: Chillers 6–8 supplied 53% of capacity and hung on the same control-card fault. With chiller 5 in maintenance, the four running units could not hold the hall.

comprehensiveAnalysis.heading: A missing line in the procedure
comprehensiveAnalysis.body: The fix, power the control card off for at least five minutes, was known to the OEM but not in the emergency procedure. Finding it cost the time in which the loop passed 28°C and locked the chillers out.

comprehensiveAnalysis.heading: Lockout needs heat removed another way
comprehensiveAnalysis.body: Escaping lockout required temporary cooling and shutting equipment down. Temperatures were back in range only at 14:00 the next day.

comprehensiveAnalysis.heading: Resilience services failed first
comprehensiveAnalysis.body: ARM, Site Recovery and Backup each had a configuration or dependency that tied them to the failed zone, so customers trying to execute their continuity plans hit errors, some in East Asia as well.

comprehensiveAnalysis.heading: What the PIR does not say
comprehensiveAnalysis.body: It does not name the facility, the chiller suppliers or models, peak hall temperature, or cost. Most actions are reported completed; the Chaos Studio expansion was due December 2023.

technicalDeepDive:
Chillers tripped by a voltage dip normally restart on their own. Here the compressor control cards hung after the dip and raised a phase sequence alarm; clearing it needed a cold restart with the capacitors drained. Each minute spent finding that out let the loop warm, and above 28°C the chillers' protection blocked any restart. Breaking out of lockout needed temporary cooling and less heat: both were done, and the chillers came back.

The platform failures were configuration errors against Azure's own zone-redundancy rules: an ARM metadata store not zonal in this region, a Site Recovery workflow on a single-zone Service Bus, a Backup cross-region-restore setting, and a storage failover check that was too strict. Microsoft reports most of these fixed.

playbook.do: Have the OEM confirm control-card behaviour under voltage dips and fix it
Map each chiller alarm code to its recovery step in the procedure
Cold-restart hung control cards at once, power off for at least five minutes
Confirm every chiller is back before restoring IT load

modes.function: Get tripped chillers running again quickly

modes.effect: Hours lost until supplier technicians arrive

rationale.S: Its gap let the loop reach lockout: 8.

rationale.D: No drill exposed the missing step.

modes.revisedRationale: Both actions are reported completed and directly close the gap.

playbook.do: Review emergency procedures with the OEM for every alarm the HMI can raise

Keep OEM technicians on call with a response time shorter than lockout

playbook.do: Pre-stage temporary cooling whenever a chiller is out for maintenance
